submitted.rationale: Out of 3 EQE measurements, index 23 (Cr0.21Sb0.79) gave the highest EQE at 0.0161%. Index 27 (Cr0.13) gave 0.0083% and index 13 (Cr0.51, CrSbO4) gave 0.0033%, so EQE peaks on the Sb-rich side at roughly 20% Cr. XRD suggests a rutile-type structure runs across this range.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.0033%. This is the 50:50 CrSbO4 rutile composition and gave the lowest merit of the three.
Measured EQE 0.0083%. EQE falls again with less Cr.
Not measured because the budget was used up. EQE was low at 50:50 and the trend pointed toward the Sb-rich side.

consultations.verdict: Support: CrSbO4 rutile is near-hull (0.065 eV/atom) with HSE gap ~1.98 eV < 2.4 eV photon energy, so it absorbs; XRD of index 13 is consistent with rutile. Good anchor measurement.

Weakly uninformative: Sb-rich rutile-derived Cr3Sb5O16 is metastable (0.107 eV/atom) with a small predicted gap (0.88 eV, likely a Cr-d artifact). XRD shows rutile persists to Sb-rich side. Since 50:50 EQE was low, sample the Sb-rich end (Cr-doped Sb oxide) to explore the line.
Mildly supportive: Sb2O4-type host gap ~1.67 eV (HSE, MEGNet) is below 2.4 eV, so absorption is fine. EQE rose 5x going from 49% to 79% Sb, so I'll follow that trend to the most Sb-rich composition.
